chapter: Last years of the band and reflections
title: Working with Jeter and Charles for thirteen years
summary: Pillars explains that Jeter ran the business while he handled the music and recruiting, and he expresses gratitude to Charles.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Okay, let me ask you a question about your relationship then.
To me, that's a long time for two people to work together and have a band and maintain the kind of relationship that you and Mr. Jeter maintained.

Yeah. Well, Jeta -- I tell you, we got along this way. He took care of all the business of the band, paid the guys off. I was in charge of the music end of the band. If I saw a musician I thought the band -- was good enough for the band, I picked him out and tell everybody, I think we should get this guy, get that guy. I did the recruiting. And a lot of times we would have a few arguments. And things just weren't rosy all the time.

But I understood him and I think he understood me, see. And my brother, Charles, was a great help with us, although he didn't share in the gravy of the band. There was very little gravy for the band, you see. But there were times when we would give him a little extra or something here or something there, see.

But I really wish it had been so we should have done -- and frankly speaking, I really feel that the two of us for him, could have done more A being honest about it. And he stuck with us right through. That's why I feel --
I saw the potential in the band.

He was with us all the way. And that's why I feel today, there's nothing I got that's too good for him. I don't know whether he knows that. But that's just the way I feel today and I'll feel that way for the rest of my life. I feel indebted to him. I really do.
It must have been a good 13 years.
